title: Fourth Constable's History
full_text:
The Fourth Constable related:

'A dishonest guardian claimed that his orphan nephew’s inheritance of thirty thousand dinars had been lost when a merchant ship sank off the coast of Alexandria. The weeping boy was left in poverty.

I did not accept the guardian’s word. I rode to Alexandria, audited the imperial custom-house ledgers for that entire year, and discovered that the ship had never sunk at all; it had arrived safely, and the guardian had sold the cargo under an assumed name to a Venetian merchant!

I seized the guardian’s estates, restored the entire thirty thousand dinars with interest to the orphan youth, and placed the corrupt uncle in the stocks, proving that verified records protect the innocent.'
moral: Documented truth and scrupulous records dismantle the most arrogant lies.
